steps.activity: Receive and document allegation — source (exception report, tip, CCTV), subject employee(s), initial evidence summary, and estimated loss value

Conduct integrity interview (with HR witness present) — present evidence, obtain written statement, document admission or denial
Determine disciplinary action in consultation with HR and Legal — options range from written warning to termination, criminal complaint, or civil recovery
Process recovery — deduct from final pay (within DOLE limits), file insurance claim if applicable, issue demand letter for civil recovery
Close case — update case management system, archive evidence per retention policy, generate lessons-learned summary, update exception rules if new pattern identified

steps.activity: Conduct unannounced dock audit — verify incoming shipment against PO and ASN: unit count, SKU accuracy, weight verification, condition assessment; compare vendor delivery vehicle manifest against system PO

Quarterly dock security assessment — evaluate physical security (locking gates, CCTV coverage, scales calibration), receiving clerk procedures compliance, and vendor credential verification

fields.Trigger: Weekly exception report showing anomalous discount activity; or cashier discount override spike; or loyalty program redemption anomaly
fields.Volume: ~33.6M annual POS transactions; ~6 promotional events/year (per W13) with coupon activity; estimated 0.1–0.3% discount abuse rate

workflows.name: Coupon & Promotional Discount Abuse Detection, Pattern Analysis & Prevention

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scan per W112" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews weekly discount exception report" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "discount type, customer" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: BuildRight Depot runs bi-monthly sale events per W13 and loyalty exclusive promotions that generate high coupon and discount activity across 200 stores and 600 POS terminals. Promotional discount abuse takes many forms: (a) cashiers applying employee or trade discounts to non-qualifying customers (sweethearting per W842), (b) customers using expired or photocopied coupons, (c) cashiers stacking multiple discount codes that should not be combinable, (d) loyalty members sharing account credentials to pool points for higher-tier discounts, (e) employees using their own loyalty account for customer purchases to accumulate personal points, and (f) repeat coupon use beyond stated limits. With promotional discounts representing 3–5% of revenue (~PHP 2–3B/year), even a 0.1% abuse rate costs BuildRight PHP 2–3M annually. This workflow focuses specifically on detecting, analyzing, and preventing coupon and promotional discount abuse patterns.
Controls: - CTL-310 (ensure controlled execution — Exception Monitoring & Investigation (PA-23.1).)
- operational: system controls that close technical loopholes (e.g., coupon stacking restrictions and usage limits)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer service vs. control trade-off** — stricter discount controls (biometric authorization, unique codes) slow checkout and frustrate legitimate customers, especially during peak sale events

- **Cashier manipulation** — experienced cashiers who understand the POS system can circumvent controls (e.g., splitting a transaction to apply coupon twice); system controls must close technical loopholes
- **Loyalty account sharing is difficult to detect** — family members sharing a single loyalty account is common in Philippine retail and hard to distinguish from abuse
- **False positives** — legitimate high-value transactions with large discounts (trade accounts, project sales) may be flagged, consuming investigation time and potentially offending good customers
Staffing Implication: - **LP Analyst**: ~3 hours/week on pattern analysis + ~10 hours/month on investigations + ~4 hours/month on prevention = ~30 hours/month; absorbed
- **LP Operations Manager**: ~2 hours/event on post-mortem + case review; absorbed
- **No incremental headcount**
System Touchpoints: - POS discount monitoring engine — real-time exception detection for discount anomalies (W1475.1)
- Discount exception report — weekly report by cashier, store, discount type, and pattern (W1475.2)
- CCTV integration per W838 — POS transaction linked to camera footage for visual investigation (W1475.3)
- POS system configuration — coupon rules, stacking restrictions, usage limits, manager authorization thresholds (W1475.4)
- Loyalty system — account activity monitoring, points anomaly detection, account sharing indicators (W1475.2)
- Integration with W842 (sweethearting), W838 (CCTV), W13 (promotions), W112 (trade pricing), W5B (POS transaction), W17 (loyalty)

steps.activity: **Automated discount exception monitoring**: System continuously monitors POS transactions for discount anomalies: (a) **Employee discount misuse**: transactions with employee discount applied but customer is not verified employee; (b) **Trade discount abuse**: trade discount rate applied without trade account scan per W112; (c) **Coupon stacking**: multiple discount codes applied to single transaction exceeding authorized total discount %; (d) **Promo code reuse**: same coupon code scanned > stated usage limit per customer; (e) **Price override patterns**: cashier price overrides > 20% below SRP per W5B requiring manager authorization — frequency by cashier; (f) **Loyalty points manipulation**: loyalty account with points accumulation spike inconsistent with purchase pattern

**Weekly pattern analysis**: LP Analyst reviews weekly discount exception report: (a) top 20 cashiers by discount exception rate (discounts applied ÷ total transactions); (b) top 20 stores by promotional discount variance (actual discount % vs. planned discount % per W13 campaign); (c) loyalty accounts with anomalous points activity (earning spikes, rapid redemption, account sharing indicators — multiple phone numbers, multiple store locations); (d) coupon code usage patterns — codes used beyond geographic or time restrictions; (e) LP Analyst categorizes exceptions: systemic (policy gap), individual (single cashier/customer), or organized (coordinated pattern)

**Individual case investigation**: For flagged exceptions: (a) LP Analyst pulls transaction detail: timestamp, store, terminal, cashier, items, discount type, customer (if loyalty/ trade); (b) review CCTV footage at POS terminal per W838 for visual confirmation (cashier behavior, customer interaction, coupon presentation); (c) interview Cashier and Department Supervisor: was the discount appropriate? was manager authorization obtained? (d) if confirmed abuse: (i) employee — disciplinary action per HR policy (verbal warning for first offense, written warning for second, termination for third), (ii) customer — flag loyalty account, restrict future coupon usage, (iii) coupon code — deactivate and notify Marketing

**Systemic prevention measures**: LP Analyst recommends preventive controls based on pattern analysis: (a) POS system configuration changes: (i) hard-code coupon exclusions (cannot stack with other discounts), (ii) enforce coupon usage limits per customer (tracked by loyalty account or phone number), (iii) require manager biometric authorization for discounts > 15%; (b) process changes: (i) daily coupon code rotation (codes change daily, texted to registered customers), (ii) trade discount requires trade account card scan (no manual entry), (iii) employee discount restricted to employee's own purchases only (verified by employee ID + biometric); (c) Marketing campaign design changes: (i) unique single-use coupon codes instead of generic codes, (ii) digital coupons delivered via app (not printable) to prevent photocopying

**Promotional event post-mortem**: After each bi-monthly sale event per W13: (a) LP Analyst compiles discount abuse report: total discount exceptions, confirmed abuse cases, financial impact (over-discount amount), policy violations by type; (b) LP Operations Manager reviews with Marketing and Store Operations: (i) were promotional terms clear and enforceable? (ii) did store staff understand discount rules? (iii) what system controls prevented abuse? (iv) what new abuse patterns emerged?; (c) incorporate lessons learned into next promotional event design per W13

workflows.name: Gift Card & Store Credit Fraud Detection, Balance Manipulation Investigation & Controls

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts receiving disproportionate store credit from returns" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews each alert" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-flag of "flag the card" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: BuildRight Depot issues gift cards and store credit (e.g., customer refund issued as store credit instead of cash per W12, referral rewards per W1472, promotional giveaways). While gift cards and store credit are important customer retention tools, they are also common fraud vectors in retail: (a) employees creating fake returns to issue store credit to their own accounts, (b) cashiers activating gift cards without collecting payment (passing the activated card to accomplices), (c) customers using stolen credit cards to purchase gift cards (converting stolen card funds to untraceable store credit), (d) manipulation of store credit balances through system exploits, and (e) social engineering — callers claiming to be customers requesting balance transfers. With ~PHP 20–30M in outstanding gift card and store credit balances, fraud directly erodes BuildRight's margin. This workflow manages detection, investigation, and prevention of gift card and store credit fraud.
Controls: - CTL-310 (ensure controlled execution — Exception Monitoring & Investigation (PA-23.1).)
- operational: LP Operations Manager review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Gift card as money laundering tool** — purchased with stolen credit cards and used to buy merchandise that is then resold; difficult to prevent without real-time card verification
- **Employee collusion** — store credit fraud requires collusion between cashier (fictitious return) and accomplice (redeeming store credit); dual-person controls help but add processing time
- **Customer experience impact** — 24-hour cooling period for store credit penalizes legitimate customers who want to use their refund immediately
- **Social engineering** — callers impersonating customers to request balance transfers are difficult to verify without strong authentication (knowledge-based authentication questions)
Staffing Implication: - **LP Analyst**: ~10–20 hours/month on case triage and investigation; absorbed
- **IT POS Administrator**: ~2 hours/month on containment and control implementation; absorbed
- **LP Operations Manager**: ~4 hours/quarter on control review; absorbed
- **No incremental headcount**
System Touchpoints: - Gift card/store credit monitoring engine — real-time fraud detection with velocity, balance, and geographic alerts (W1476.1)
- Transaction history module — complete gift card/store credit audit trail from issuance to redemption (W1476.2)
- Account freeze capability — IT can freeze suspected compromised accounts instantly (W1476.3)
- Gift card liability reconciliation — daily balance verification vs. GL (W1476.5)
- POS system controls — activation limits, manager authorization, cooling periods (W1476.5)
- Integration with W838 (CCTV), W842 (cash handling exceptions), W12 (returns/store credit), W17 (loyalty), W5B (POS transaction)

steps.activity: **Automated fraud monitoring**: System monitors gift card and store credit transactions for fraud indicators: (a) **Velocity alerts**: single gift card loaded with > PHP 10,000 in a single transaction; multiple gift cards activated on same terminal within 1 hour; (b) **Return-credit pattern**: employee-associated loyalty accounts receiving disproportionate store credit from returns (indicator of fictitious return scheme); (c) **Balance anomaly**: gift card balance increasing without corresponding purchase transaction; store credit balance changed outside normal system processes; (d) **Geographic impossibility**: same gift card/store credit used at two different stores simultaneously or within an implausible travel time; (e) **Payment method risk**: gift cards purchased with credit cards subsequently reported as fraudulent (chargeback risk)

**Case triage & investigation**: LP Analyst reviews each alert: (a) confirm anomaly is genuine (not system error or legitimate unusual transaction — e.g., a contractor legitimately purchasing PHP 50,000 in gift cards for project giveaways); (b) for confirmed suspicious activity: (i) pull complete transaction history for the gift card/store credit account, (ii) identify the CSR/cashier who processed the transaction, (iii) review CCTV footage per W838 for the transaction timestamp, (iv) cross-reference with other fraud indicators — is the same cashier or store appearing in multiple alerts? (c) categorize fraud type: employee fraud, external fraud (stolen cards), system exploit, social engineering

**Immediate containment**: (a) for active fraud in progress: IT POS Administrator freezes the affected gift card/store credit account to prevent further use; (b) for suspected employee involvement: Store Manager removes cashier from POS duties pending investigation per HR policy; (c) for suspected stolen credit card purchases: LP Analyst notifies payment gateway to flag the card; (d) for system exploit: IT applies emergency patch to close the vulnerability
steps.r: IT POS Administrator / Store Manager / LP Analyst

steps.activity: **Investigation resolution & recovery**: (a) if fraud confirmed: (i) **Employee fraud**: HR disciplinary process — repayment of stolen amount or termination per W19.5 separation; report to LP database; (ii) **External fraud**: file police report for stolen credit card activity; block customer account; if identity discovered, pursue civil recovery; (iii) **System exploit**: IT fixes vulnerability; quantify financial impact; Finance writes off unrecoverable loss; (b) LP Analyst documents case with evidence, resolution, and financial impact in LP case management system

**Quarterly control review & system hardening**: (a) LP Operations Manager reviews all gift card/store credit fraud cases from prior quarter: patterns, root causes, financial impact; (b) recommend system controls: (i) gift card activation requires manager authorization for values > PHP 5,000, (ii) store credit issuance requires supervisor approval and customer ID verification, (iii) daily reconciliation of gift card liability account (total cards outstanding × balances) vs. GL per W86, (iv) two-person control for bulk gift card activation (promotional giveaways), (v) store credit refund timeout — 24-hour hold before store credit can be used (cooling period to detect fraudulent returns); (c) IT implements approved controls

fields.Participants: LP Director, Regional LP Officers, Store Managers, IT Security, Legal Counsel, Philippine National Police (PNP)
fields.Trigger: Exception-based reporting (EBR) system identifies pattern of related theft incidents across multiple stores; or LP Officer reports suspected organized ring
fields.Volume: Each investigation may involve 3–10 stores and PHP 500K–5M in losses

workflows.name: Organized Retail Crime (ORC) Pattern Detection, Multi-Store Correlation & Law Enforcement Coordination

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates ORC alert with supporting data" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews ORC alert" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "logs, exception reports, and inventory variance data" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: Organized Retail Crime (ORC) involves coordinated theft by professional groups targeting specific high-value categories — power tools, copper wire, branded adhesives, and high-end fixtures at BuildRight. Unlike opportunistic shoplifting, ORC rings operate across multiple stores and regions, use sophisticated methods (receipt fraud, barcode swapping, distraction teams), and resell stolen goods through informal markets or online platforms. Detecting ORC requires correlating incidents across stores and time periods, which is impossible with single-store analysis. This workflow governs the specialized process of ORC detection, investigation, and law enforcement coordination.
Controls: - CTL-310 (ensure controlled execution — Exception Monitoring & Investigation (PA-23.1).)
- operational: LP Director review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Evidence admissibility**: Philippine courts have strict rules on evidence chain of custody; CCTV footage must be properly timestamped, stored, and documented to be admissible
- **Employee safety**: ORC rings may threaten or intimidate store employees who cooperate with investigations; LP must ensure employee safety protocols are in place
- **Cross-jurisdiction complexity**: ORC rings operating across Philippine regions (Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao) require coordination with multiple PNP regional commands
Staffing Implication: - LP Director: ~50% of time on ORC investigations and oversight; dedicated role
- Regional LP Officers (20): provide evidence gathering support as part of regional duties; dedicated positions
- No incremental headcount
System Touchpoints: - Multi-store pattern detection engine with cross-correlation algorithms (W1542.1)
- Secure investigation file management with role-based access restriction (W1542.2–3)
- CCTV timestamp correlation with POS transaction logs (W1542.3)
- EBR system ORC pattern library for continuous learning (W1542.7)
Time Estimate: - Pattern detection review: 2 hours/alert × ~20 alerts/year = 40 hours
- Investigation: 20–40 hours per investigation × ~8 cases/year = 160–320 hours
- Law enforcement coordination: 8–16 hours per case

steps.activity: **Pattern detection**: System analyzes loss patterns across all 200 stores — (a) same SKU category with unusual shrinkage spikes at ≥ 3 stores within 30 days, (b) same vehicle/license plate at multiple store loading zones, (c) similar suspicious transaction patterns (excessive returns without receipt, repeated high-value voids by same cashier), (d) CCTV correlation of same individuals at multiple stores; generates ORC alert with supporting data

**Investigation activation**: LP Director reviews ORC alert; classifies investigation priority — High (losses > PHP 1M or suspected internal collusion), Medium (PHP 200K–1M), Low (< PHP 200K); assigns lead investigator; creates confidential investigation file restricted from store-level access

**Multi-store evidence gathering**: Regional LP Officers at affected stores pull CCTV footage, transaction logs, exception reports, and inventory variance data; IT Security extracts digital evidence (access logs, transaction timestamps, POS override records); all evidence consolidated in secure investigation file

**Suspect identification & surveillance**: For High-priority investigations, LP Director authorizes enhanced surveillance at targeted stores — additional CCTV monitoring, undercover LP presence, vehicle tracking (if warranted and legally permissible); coordinates with store management to maintain normal operations during surveillance

**Law enforcement coordination**: For confirmed ORC cases with sufficient evidence, LP Director coordinates with PNP Criminal Investigation Division — submits formal complaint with evidence dossier (CCTV footage, transaction records, inventory reports); Legal Counsel reviews to ensure BuildRight's reporting obligations are met and employee rights are protected

**Internal collusion investigation** (if applicable): If evidence suggests employee involvement (e.g., cashier processing fraudulent voids, receiving clerk facilitating theft), LP Director coordinates with HR for employee investigation per W79 (grievance process); ensures due process while maintaining investigation integrity; employee suspension pending investigation per DOLE requirements

**Case closure & prevention measures**: Upon case resolution (arrest, recovery, or closure), LP Director documents lessons learned; implements targeted prevention measures — enhanced CCTV angles at affected areas, POS procedure changes, vendor collaboration for product tagging; updates ORC pattern library in EBR system for future detection improvement
